findings.title: Google refresh persists the Zod result wrapper as the credential
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse object ({success, data}), not the parsed token. This call site used to store googleCredentialSchema.parse(...), but now writes that wrapper to credential.key (lines 97-100). The in-memory client is updated from googleCredentials, so the current request can still succeed, but the next load runs googleCredentialSchema.parse on {success, data} and throws. Every Google Calendar credential breaks after the first refresh (about an hour), with or without credential sync. If sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response with no .data, so token.access_token throws; the catch on line 108 treats any error other than invalid_grant as success and returns the expired client, so refresh fails silently and the credential is not marked invalid.

findings.title: Salesforce token update calls prisma but never imports it
findings.body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update after refreshing the Salesforce token, but this file does not import prisma. The name is undefined, so the first Salesforce calendar operation throws ReferenceError once the token endpoint returns OK and never builds a jsforce Connection. Salesforce event create/update/delete is broken for every user as soon as this ships, including installs that never enable credential sync.

findings.title: Refresh parser strips real tokens and writes a fake refresh_token
findings.body: The minimum schema's computed keys are z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString(), not wildcards. Those are literal property names (both typically "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first). They do not match expires_in or expiry_date. When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, every caller uses this schema, including team credentials that still hit the real provider (the switch does not check whether the sync fetch ran) and Salesforce, which never calls the sync endpoint. safeParse then keeps only access_token and strips refresh_token and expiry. Lines 25-27 set refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" whenever it is missing. Office 365 spreads that object over the stored credential (office365calendar CalendarService.ts around line 264) and saves it, replacing the real refresh token. Zoom assigns newTokens.refresh_token and does Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000, so expiry_date becomes NaN/null and the refresh token is destroyed. The same fake value is applied on the default path whenever the app schema leaves refresh_token optional, which Office 365 does, and the refresh request does not send offline_access, so a response that omits refresh_token permanently breaks reconnect-free refresh.

findings.title: Salesforce now fails closed on an unconditional, wrong-host token refresh
findings.body: getClient always POSTs to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token before returning a connection, even when the stored access token is still valid. Sandbox and many My Domain orgs must refresh against test.salesforce.com or their own login host; login.salesforce.com rejects those refresh tokens. Failure is detected via statusText !== "OK" (not response.ok), the error body is discarded, and the credential is not marked invalid, so the throw aborts every Salesforce operation instead of falling back to the existing token. The Connection on lines 101-108 is still built with credentialKey.access_token and credentialKey.instance_url, not the token just fetched, so a successful refresh is not what the client uses. Adding the missing prisma import does not fix this.

findings.title: Sync refresh returns a raw fetch Response callers cannot consume
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the fetch Response and does not check response.ok or parse JSON. Callers were not updated to that contract, and the comment says the body should be only an access token and expiry, which none of them read. Google expects a gaxios response and reads res.data (throws, then swallowed). Hubspot expects a token object with expiresIn/accessToken and then prisma-updates that value as credential.key; a Response JSON-serializes to an empty or near-empty object, so a refresh can wipe the Hubspot credential. Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read axios .data and throw. Lark passes the Response to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's {code, data} envelope. Webex still validates with webexRefreshedTokenSchema (fixed scope, refresh_token, refresh_token_expires_in), so the documented minimal body is rejected. Office 365 video replaces the entire credential key with the parsed body, so a partial payload drops refresh_token and email. With the feature env vars set, token refresh for these apps fails or destroys stored credentials.

findings.title: Token sync request is unauthenticated
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug. It does not send CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, a bearer token, or a body signature, and the URL scheme is not required to be HTTPS. The inbound webhook is authenticated, but this outbound call is what returns live OAuth access tokens. The parent app cannot tell Cal.com from any other caller, and user ids are sequential, so anyone who can reach that URL can request access tokens for arbitrary users. A self-hoster cannot fix that without editing this shared helper.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sync sends the credential id as the user id
findings.body: refreshAccessToken is only given credentialId (the credential primary key) and passes that value as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens. When sync is enabled the helper treats any truthy number as a user id and posts it as calcomUserId, so the parent looks up the wrong user (or nobody) and will not return this user's token. The normal axios refresh is skipped entirely in that mode. The caller also expects an axios response (tokenInfo.data on line 96); a fetch Response has no .data, so the refresh throws even if the endpoint responded.

findings.title: Lark deletes the credential before credential sync can refresh it
findings.body: The new sync call sits after the guard that deletes the credential when refresh_token is missing or refresh_expires_date is expired. Credential sync is the path that is supposed to obtain a new access token from the parent when Cal.com does not hold a usable refresh token (parseRefreshTokenResponse even fabricates refresh_token because sync responses may omit it). A webhook-created Lark credential without a still-valid refresh token is deleted on first use instead of being refreshed, and the user must reconnect. If a refresh token is present, the sync Response is still passed to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's envelope, so a normal token JSON body fails the refresh anyway.

findings.title: Credential webhook updates an arbitrary row and leaves it invalid
findings.body: The handler findFirsts on userId plus appId with no orderBy, then updates or creates outside a transaction. userId and appId are not unique: Google's callback always inserts a new credential, and calendar code later loads a specific credential id. findFirst can update a different row than the one in use, return 200, and leave the active token stale. Concurrent deliveries can both miss and insert duplicates. The update only writes key, so a row already marked invalid stays invalid and is skipped by calendar loading even after a successful sync. Decrypted keys are JSON.parsed and stored with no per-app schema check, so a payload that is not the shape that app expects is persisted and breaks the integration on next use.

findings.title: Zoom sync asks for app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with appSlug "zoomvideo", but the Zoom app id and installed slug are "zoom" (see zoomvideo/api/callback.ts, appId: "zoom"). Other integrations pass the app-store slug (google-calendar, msteams, office365-calendar). The webhook stores credentials under appMetadata.slug, so a parent that keys off the real slug will not find a Zoom credential when Cal.com posts appSlug=zoomvideo, and token refresh for Zoom sync will 404 or return the wrong app's tokens.

findings.title: No tests for credential ingestion or the shared refresh path
findings.body: The new webhook can overwrite any user's OAuth credentials, and parseRefreshTokenResponse / refreshOAuthTokens now run on Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce refresh. The PR checklist says tests were not added, and there are none for a missing or wrong webhook secret, decrypt failure, two credentials for one app, or a refresh that reloads the saved key. A round-trip that refreshes a Google credential and reads it back would have caught the safeParse wrapper being stored; an Office 365 refresh whose body omits refresh_token would have caught the literal "refresh_token" overwrite.
